The base image `FROM alpine AS base` is using the implicit `latest` tag, which is a mutable reference and introduces supply-chain risk if the upstream image is compromised or changed unexpectedly. An attacker who gains control over the `alpine` image or registry could impact all future builds without any Dockerfile change. Pin this base image to a specific version tag or immutable digest to ensure reproducible and trustworthy builds.

There's no validation to prevent duplicate section IDs from different plugins. If two plugins return sections with the same ID, this could cause issues with the expand/collapse state tracking (which uses `plugin_${section.id}` as keys) and potentially confuse users. The collapsible logic is inconsistent with existing sidebar sections. Other sections (MCP, LSP, diff, todo) only become collapsible when they have more than 2 items, but plugin sections use `collapsible !== false && items.length > 2`. This means a plugin section with `collapsible: undefined` and 3 items will be collapsible, while a section with `collapsible: true` and 2 items won't be. Consider using just `section.collapsible !== false` to respect the plugin's intent, or enforce the same `> 2` rule consistently.
```suggestion
                const isCollapsible = () => section.items.length > 2 && section.collapsible !== false
```
